clue.text: One's accompanying the Queen visiting military hospital and mess

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so the pair of pieces sits inside the hospital

parts.note: MASH is a Mobile Army Surgical Hospital, as in the TV series

indicators.note: keeping company with, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: one is, written as I'S
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A royal tour of an army field hospital and its dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the military dining room of the surface, but it is a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch or muddle of things is a mess, a jumbled confusion.

clue.text: Fungus, note, will, finally, before the day's up

indicators.note: coming ahead of, so the earlier pieces precede this one

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the end of the word will is taken
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: WED is short for Wednesday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: A list of items before someone's day comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a thin whitish mould growing on plants or damp surfaces.

clue.text: Thursday broadcast's before 9

indicators.note: comes ahead, so this piece goes first

parts.note: to strew is to scatter seed, broadcasting it

explanation.surface: A programme goes out on Thursday ahead of nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is a cross-reference to the answer at 9 across, another exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of astonishment, this one from 'God's truth'.

clue.text: What male dinosaurs could make you?

definitions.text: What male dinosaurs could make you?

indicators.note: the letters could be remade into something new

explanation.surface: Wondering what a lot of macho dinosaurs might turn you into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make you' rearranges the letters of 'dinosaurs', after M for male; 'dinosaurs' doubles as old-fashioned chauvinists in the whole-clue reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Hating men is a natural reaction to boorish 'dinosaurs', old-fashioned chauvinists.

clue.text: To get around scale, after old-fashioned drill

indicators.note: placed later, so this part follows the first

parts.note: square means conventional, out of date

indicators.note: surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to bag something is to get it
to shin up is to climb, to scale

explanation.surface: Someone learns musical scales after being trained in antiquated methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' reads as music, but it is the verb to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British military slang for parade-ground marching practice.

clue.text: Gridlocked, perhaps, in transport leaving city

indicators.note: one piece departs from the other, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to be in transports is to be ecstatic, enraptured
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Traffic seizes up as vehicles try to get out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' reads as vehicles, but it is rapture, giving ECSTATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridlocked traffic is not moving at all, an example of being stationary.

clue.text: Gather friar eats in school

definitions.meaning: to fold fabric into a pleat
British school slang for snacks and sweets

explanation.surface: A monk collects his school dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck means a pleat, is the name of Robin Hood's friar, and is boarding-school food.

clue.text: Born bully?

parts.note: a natural thug, read as someone born under the sign of the Bull

explanation.definitionFit: A person born under Taurus, the Bull, is 'bully' in the punning astrological sense.

clue.text: Commander leading a team reaching peak in S America

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
top means leading, foremost
XI is eleven, a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: An officer heads a squad up to a South American summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotopaxi is an active volcano in the Andes of Ecuador.

clue.text: My part reduced after reflecting

indicators.note: a mirror image runs backwards, so the shortened word is read in reverse
cut down, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders and decides to scale back their contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise; 'Lor' is a dialect form of Lord, like 'My!'

clue.text: Vegetable to go after in place of game

parts.note: a squash is a gourd such as a marrow
to court is to pursue or woo

explanation.surface: Someone is told to chase a vegetable in place of playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' looks like 'instead of', but 'in' is a link and 'place of game' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The walled room where squash is played is a sports venue for that racket game.

clue.text: Seeks zoom lens to snap area imposing restrictions

indicators.note: snapping breaks things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A photographer hunts for a telephoto lens to photograph a restricted zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' reads as taking a photo, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A district where burning coal and other smoky fuels is banned by law.

clue.text: Dickensian orphan Twist in desperate reversal, having no one

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
lacking something, so that letter is dropped
turning round, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a do-or-die effort is a desperate one
I is the Roman numeral for one
to wind is to twist or coil

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist, the other Dickens orphan, caught in a desperate turn of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' points at Oliver Twist, but it is WIND. 'reversal' turns DO OR DIE to EIDROOD, 'having no one' removes I to give EDROOD, and WIND goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Dickens's unfinished last novel is a young man whose parents are both dead.

clue.text: Work for a while that doctor may take, briefly

definitions.meaning: to work as a temporary office worker
a doctor takes your temperature; briefly says it is shortened

explanation.surface: A short-term job that a doctor might accept for a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a stand-in worker hired for a limited period, and the abbreviation also stands for a fever reading.

clue.text: Expend least effort, as chiropodists do without hesitation

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: foot doctors trim corns, the hard patches on toes
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Foot specialists working without pausing to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp by taking shortcuts is to do the minimum work possible.

clue.text: Legendary red ointment for child that's really dear

parts.note: Che Guevara, the iconic revolutionary, a famous communist or red
a rub is a liniment or salve

explanation.surface: A mythical red balm for a beloved child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legendary red' suggests folklore, but it is the revolutionary hero Che.
explanation.definitionFit: An angelic-looking, adorable little one is often called a little angel or cherub.

clue.text: March features one short horse with bullock following?

indicators.note: coming after, so this piece is placed at the end
cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: equine means relating to horses, used here as a noun for a horse
a bullock is a castrated ox

explanation.surface: A procession includes a stubby horse with a bullock trailing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a parade, but it is the month containing the spring equinox.
explanation.definitionFit: The vernal point when day and night are of equal length falls around 20 March.

clue.text: Chap getting publicity free, still concentrating on features?

parts.note: he is any male person
an ad is an advertisement
to be shot of something is to be rid of it, free

explanation.surface: A man gets free advertising yet still focuses on articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'nevertheless', but it is a photograph; 'features' are a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait photo of the face is a still picture focused on someone's looks.

clue.text: These usen't to get worked up about harmful emission?

definitions.text: These usen't to get worked up about harmful emission?

indicators.note: surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
agitated, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: CO is carbon monoxide, a poisonous exhaust gas

explanation.surface: Environmental zealots who used not to fuss about pollution now do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get worked up' rearranges the letters of usen't into ENUTS; read whole, the clue describes the green campaigners themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Green campaigners obsessed with pollution are fittingly described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Wrong start, therefore ignoring that

parts.note: 'they're off' is the start of a race

indicators.note: disregarding the start just mentioned, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: hence means therefore, for that reason

explanation.surface: A false start, so disregard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring that' refers back to 'start': HENCE without its start leaves ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong is a crime or transgression, an illegal act.

clue.text: Exotic bit of verse could go oddly astray

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters go missing, so only the even ones of these words remain

explanation.surface: A strange line of poetry that might wander off course.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the run VERSECOULDGO, losing the odd letters leaves the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro, a foreign coin.

clue.text: Readily accept doctor, popular with family

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Welcoming a well-liked GP who gets on with one's relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb eagerly what one sees or hears, taking it all in.

clue.text: A house and a car for one turning heads

indicators.note: goes at the head of, so this piece comes first
turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: eg, for example
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A home and a vehicle for a single person that make people look.
explanation.walkthrough: In astrology a 'house' is one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is one of the twelve astrological houses or signs.

clue.text: Pants one would be expecting to be up!

definitions.text: one would be expecting to be up!
definitions.meaning: a woman expecting a baby is 'up the' this word, slang for pregnant

explanation.definitionFit: Duff is British slang for useless or broken, and the phrase 'up the duff' means pregnant.

clue.text: Insults mate with false respect

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, impudence
a stallion services a mare, mating with her

explanation.surface: Someone abuses a friend while pretending to show esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' reads as a friend, but it is the verb used of breeding animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying lip service means expressing support or regard you do not really hold.

clue.text: City just to the west of delta in ricefields

definitions.text: just to the west of delta in ricefields
definitions.meaning: in the word ricefields the letter before D (delta) is L, called by this name in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A town sitting next to a river delta among paddy fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell RICEFIELDS in the NATO alphabet: the code word just before Delta is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the Peruvian capital, and also the radio code word for the letter L.

clue.text: Very close, offering affection

parts.note: handing something over is offering it
love is deep affection

explanation.surface: Two people extremely intimate, giving each other tenderness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people working in intimate collusion, inseparably allied.

clue.text: Put out, I carp

parts.note: KO is a knockout, putting a boxer out cold

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they are annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the verb to complain, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Koi are ornamental Japanese fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Something digital newspaper makes undesirable

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: An online paper turns out to be a nasty thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computers, but it means relating to digits. Toerag is British slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, an undesirable is an unwelcome person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: City brothels in kinky shows

indicators.note: displays, so the letters are exposed within these words

explanation.surface: A town's bordellos put on perverse performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.
